title: Valid Word Square
summary: Determine if an array of strings forms a valid word square by checking if the kth row and column match for all k.
statement: Determine if an array of strings forms a valid word square by checking if the kth row and column match for all k.
constraints: 1 <= words.length <= 500; each word has 1–500 lowercase English letters.
Rows may have different lengths. Every kth row must match the kth column, including character count.
Check the given rows in their existing order; do not rearrange them.
hints: Every existing character needs a matching character at the transposed position.
Check both bounds before comparing words[row][col] with words[col][row].
For each character, reject if the other row is missing, too short, or has a different character.
Mirror checks accept symmetric ragged shapes and reject missing entries. Full-square dimensions are not required.
editorial: If every character has an equal transposed partner, each row and column has the same characters at the same positions. Missing mirrored positions invalidate the square. Do not use zip to truncate to the shortest row, and do not require every row to have n characters. Each given character is checked once with constant extra storage.

tests.explanation: Each row equals its corresponding column: for example row 1 and column 1 both read bnrt.
This ragged arrangement is valid: its row and column lengths are both 4,4,3,2, with matching letters.
